title: Low optical receive power

scenario.title: Low optical receive power
scenario.short: DOM warning on a switch receiver; link still up.

path.text: srv-a eth0 → CBL-F101 → pp-01 F01 → [PP-01 F01⇄R01] → pp-01 R01 → TRK-0102-P1 → pp-02 R01 → [PP-02 R01⇄F01] → pp-02 F01 → CBL-F201 → asw-1 Ethernet1/1

initial_symptom: Monitoring: DOM low-warning on asw-1 Ethernet1/1 receive power. No user-facing outage reported yet.

baseline.title: Optical telemetry — asw-1:Ethernet1/1 ⇄ srv-a:eth0
baseline.interpretation: asw-1:Ethernet1/1: Rx -3.10 dBm within its module thresholds. srv-a:eth0: Rx -3.50 dBm within its module thresholds. Estimated loss srv-a:eth0 → asw-1:Ethernet1/1: 1.30 dB vs. documented planning budget ≈ 1.30 dB. Estimated loss asw-1:Ethernet1/1 → srv-a:eth0: 1.30 dB vs. documented planning budget ≈ 1.30 dB.
baseline.command: show interface Ethernet1/1 transceiver details ; [srv-a:eth0] ethtool -m eth0

baseline.title: Reachability srv-a → srv-b (IPv4, 56 B, ×10)
baseline.interpretation: All 10 probes from srv-a to 192.0.2.12 were answered (56-byte payload). This confirms IP reachability for packets of this size in both directions at the time of the test. It does not prove that larger packets, sustained throughput, or other flows work.

baseline.title: Throughput srv-a → srv-b (10s, P1)
baseline.interpretation: Average 23.31 Gbit/s over 10 s with 0 retransmissions on a 25 Gbit/s path (MSS 8960).

diagnostic_actions.title: Monitoring alarm — DOM Rx low-warning (asw-1 Ethernet1/1)
diagnostic_actions.interpretation: A monitoring threshold crossing is the trigger for investigation, not a diagnosis.

diagnostic_actions.title: Optical telemetry — asw-1:Ethernet1/1 ⇄ srv-a:eth0
diagnostic_actions.interpretation: asw-1:Ethernet1/1: Rx -11.50 dBm is below this module's low-warning threshold (-9.90 dBm). srv-a:eth0: Rx -3.50 dBm within its module thresholds. Estimated loss srv-a:eth0 → asw-1:Ethernet1/1: 9.70 dB vs. documented planning budget ≈ 1.30 dB. Estimated loss asw-1:Ethernet1/1 → srv-a:eth0: 1.30 dB vs. documented planning budget ≈ 1.30 dB. Low receive power is evidence of a degraded optical path toward that receiver. It does not by itself identify the failed component: candidates include a contaminated or damaged connector, excess loss at a mated pair or bend, a weak remote transmitter, an incorrect optic/fiber type, or a sensor error.
diagnostic_actions.command: show interface Ethernet1/1 transceiver details ; [srv-a:eth0] ethtool -m eth0

diagnostic_actions.title: Documented cable path — srv-a:eth0
diagnostic_actions.interpretation: Records show 3 cable segment(s) and 4 patch-panel mated connection(s) between srv-a:eth0 and asw-1:Ethernet1/1. Every mated point is a place where contamination or excess loss can occur. This is the documented path; it does not prove the physical cabling matches the records.
diagnostic_actions.command: fiberscope trace --from srv-a:eth0   # cable registry query

diagnostic_actions.title: Connector inspection — asw-1:Ethernet1/1
diagnostic_actions.interpretation: Inspection at asw-1:Ethernet1/1 (connector of CBL-F201) records a clean end-face. This point is unlikely to be the source of excess loss.
diagnostic_actions.command: inspection-record --location asw-1:Ethernet1/1   # recorded procedure, video probe

diagnostic_actions.title: Connector inspection — pp-02:F01
diagnostic_actions.interpretation: Inspection at pp-02:F01 (connector of CBL-F201) records contamination in the core zone. Contamination at a mated pair adds loss and is a plausible cause of low receive power. Recommended procedure: clean, then re-inspect before reconnecting; re-read optics afterwards.
diagnostic_actions.command: inspection-record --location pp-02:F01   # recorded procedure, video probe
